manifest.billing: standard GitHub-hosted runners are free for public repositories; Windows runners bill at 2x minutes only on private repositories
manifest.expected_upper_runner_minutes_note: worst case assumes every invocation reaches its CPU limit and its wall equals the watchdog; Stage C observed wall ~= CPU + 1% for these single-threaded solvers
manifest.job_layout: 3 static matrices (one per solver) of 130 jobs; each job = one graph, three policies sequentially on one runner
manifest.retry_rule: A job is retried only after an infrastructure failure (wall_watchdog, not_run_job_deadline, driver_error, missing_record, build_mismatch, runner loss or a failed publish). The whole job (all three policies, same order) is re-run as a new attempt via "Re-run failed jobs"; at most 2 retries. Analysis uses, per job, the first attempt without an infrastructure failure, never mixing invocations of different attempts; after 3 failed attempts the job is reported as infrastructure_failure. Solver timeouts, solver errors, policy errors and verification failures are results and are never retried. Every attempt is preserved.
manifest.runner: windows-2025 (standard GitHub-hosted, 4 vCPU); one solver process at a time per runner

timing_repetitions.eligible: jobs in which all three policies complete with CPU < 60 s
timing_repetitions.note: NOT included in max_solver_cpu_hours; proposed separately; repetitions rotate the policy order and are never used to replace primary records
